lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon asks for a sign: let me know that You will save Israel by my hand.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He prepares a young goat, unleavened cakes, and broth, and places them on the rock.

lines.speaker: angel
lines.text: Take the meat and the cakes, place them on the rock, and pour out the broth.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Angel touches the offering with the tip of the staff. Fire rises from the rock and consumes it.

lines.speaker: gideon
lines.text: Alas, O Lord God! I have seen the Angel of the Lord face to face.

lines.speaker: angel
lines.text: Peace to you. Do not fear; you shall not die.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gideon builds an altar there, and calls it The Lord Is Peace. It stands to this day in Ophrah.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That same night, Gideon tears down the altar of Baal. His father Joash defies the town: let Baal contend for himself. They name Gideon Jerubbaal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The Spirit clothes Gideon. He sounds the trumpet, and the Abiezrites gather to him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sign settles. The fire was not Gideon's doing. What remains is trust, not a rewrite.

choices.label: Rise and go
choices.note: The story keeps its shape; Gideon carries the sign forward.

choices.label: Rest by the altar
choices.note: A pause does not change the outcome. It only lets the player breathe.
